name: Name
body: Battle Forge is a monthly series that presents a new WARMACHINE scenario in each installment. Battle Forge scenarios emphasize the narrative unfolding over the course of a game and may be asymmetrical, uneven, and even somewhat experimental because the goal of Battle Forge is to create a sandbox toolset that allows for creative scenario generation and new, story-worthy experiences with WARMACHINE! Players are encouraged to modify Battle Forge scenarios in any way that makes the scenario more appropriate for their army collections and their available terrain resources. Most important of all, have fun! And if you find a better way to do something with a scenario that results in a better experience for you, let us know at feedback@privateerpress.com, so we can try it, too!

name: Name
body: Following are the key terms that will be repeated in many Battle Forge scenarios:

name: Name
body: Many scenarios utilize objectives. An objective can either be a terrain piece, a marker, or a zone designated on a terrain piece or on the map.

name: Name
body: Objective Markers are impassable terrain features and should be represented on the table with markers that are at least 20 mm in diameter. Unless otherwise specified, all Objective Markers used in a scenario should be the same size.

name: Name
body: To have more models in an area than your opponent does.

name: Name
body: An area or objective is contested if both players have models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective at a time when scoring would take place. An area or objective is uncontested if only one player has models in the area or in scoring proximity to the objective when scoring would take place.

name: Name
body: The zone or the area of a terrain feature is held when a player occupies the area with two or more models, uncontested.

name: Name
body: An objective terrain piece or marker is secured when a player has two or more models within 1" of the objective, uncontested.

name: Name
body: Battle Forge victories can be determined by either achieving the goals of the scenario or through Victory Points, scored in a variety of ways throughout playing a scenario. Turn limits on scenarios put pressure on players to succeed within a set amount of turns, and Victory Points provide the means to determine victory when neither player has completed the primary objective of a scenario.

name: Name
body:
In addition to its standard rules, each Battle Forge scenario has two random tables that add additional Victory Point-scoring opportunities for players that vary each time the scenario is played. Mission Modifiers add additional scoring opportunities based on the position of a player’s models on the table. Achievements add additional scoring opportunities based on a player’s actions taken on the battlefield.
Players should roll a d6 to randomly determine Mission Modifiers and Achievements before the beginning of a game, or players can choose them at will if all players agree. It is recommended that only one Mission Modifier and one Achievement should be in effect during any match (unless you really want to get crazy).

name: Name
body: If a player makes an attack that destroys one or more friendly models, that player’s opponent gains 1 Victory Point. If a player makes an attack and destroys their own Leader model, that player immediately loses the match.

name: Name
body: In addition to objectives, Battle Forge scenarios will routinely draw on the following terrain elements. Dimensions provided are approximations, and you should feel free to substitute any terrain pieces you have available as necessary. Use the resources you have available to get close enough to maintain the spirit and intention of the scenario.

name: Name
body: An obstacle with an approximate footprint of 3/4" x 4". Barriers provide cover.

name: Name
body: Obstructions with an approximate footprint of 5" x 5".

name: Name
body: Forest areas with an approximate footprint of 5" in diameter.

name: Name
body: An area of shallow water approximately 5" in diameter.

name: Name

name: Name
body: "March Madness" is designed for 50-point forces.

name: Name
body: "March Madness" ends after six rounds.

name: Name
body: In MARCH MADNESS, forces compete by "dunking" explosive charges into their opponent’s structures, and the player who makes the biggest explosion at the end of the match wins!

name: Name
body: Dunk more bombs into your opponent’s structure than they dunk into yours.

name: Name
body:
This scenario uses 2 Guard Towers, 4 small forests, 2 small rubble fields, 1 small pond, and 4 small barriers as shown on the table as shown on the map below. If you don’t have this exact assortment of terrain, use what you have to create a diverse environment that provides some challenging terrain in which to place the bombs. You’ll also need seven 20 mm scenario Bomb objectives.
The Bomb objectives should be placed on the map as shown.

name: Name
body:
MARCH MADNESS uses Execution Mode, meaning Leaders can only be destroyed by other Leaders.
Bombs can only be carried by Cohort models.
Cohort models can automatically pick up Bombs during any turn activation they begin their movement within, end their movement within, or advance within 1" of a Bomb. A Cohort model can only carry one Bomb at a time and cannot pick up another Bomb if it is already carrying one.
Cohort models can pass a Bomb to another friendly Cohort model within 6" by making a ranged attack targeting the friendly model. If the ranged attack hits, the target friendly Cohort model picks up the Bomb. If the attack misses, the Bomb is dropped.
Dropped Bombs — If a Cohort model misses a pass or a Cohort model carrying a Bomb is knocked down, destroyed, or removed from play, the Cohort model drops the Bomb. Place the Bomb it was carrying in B2B  contact with the Cohort model, positioned as close to the enemy structure as possible where it does not touch another model’s base, an obstruction, or an obstacle.

name: Name
body: All Cohort models gain the Dunk special rule. Dunk — A Cohort model carrying a Bomb that begins its activation within a number of inches equal to its SPD of an enemy structure gains Flight for one turn. If a Cohort model carrying a Bomb ends its activation within 1" of the enemy structure, the Bomb is deposited in the structure. Mark the structure with a Bomb token to show that a Bomb has been deposited. Bombs can only be deposited in an enemy’s structure as a result of the Dunk special rule. Players score 2 Victory Points each time one of their Cohort models deposits a Bomb in an enemy structure. Bomb Reset — If at any time all Bombs have been removed from play but the scenario has not ended by reaching a victory condition, put seven new Bombs on the map based on the original placement diagram.

name: Name
body: Roll once on both the Mission Modifiers and Achievement tables. But this is MARCH MADNESS, so why not play with all Mission Modifiers and Achievements active?!

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Mission Modifier for this match: 1. Fouled—If a Cohort model carrying a Bomb is damaged but not destroyed by an enemy attack, place the Cohort model within 3" of the enemy structure with the center of its base touching the straight line that connects the center points of both structures. The Cohort model cannot be targeted by enemy attacks for the rest of the turn. 2. Fast Break—While carrying a Bomb, friendly Cohort models gain +2 SPD if there are more friendly Cohort models than enemy Cohort models on the enemy’s side of the table. 3. Three Pointer—Unengaged Cohort models greater than 7" away from an enemy structure can attempt to deposit the Bomb by making a ranged attack against DEF 21. If the attack hits, the Bomb is deposited. If the attack misses, the Bomb is removed from play.

name: Name
body: Roll a d3 to determine the Achievement for this match. 1. Alley-Oop—Gain 1 Victory Point when your Cohort model successfully Dunks after receiving a passed Bomb from another Cohort model during the same turn. 2. Steal—Gain 1 Victory Point when your Cohort model picks up a Bomb that was carried by an enemy Cohort model in the previous turn. 3. MVP—Gain 1 Victory Point for each subsequent successful Dunk by the same Cohort model after the first successful Dunk by that model.

name: Name
body: Victory conditions are checked in the following order: Decisive Win: The first player to score 8 Victory Points wins. Point Advantage Win: At the end of any of the second player’s turns, a player with 6 or more Victory Points than their opponent wins the match. Victory Point Win: If neither player has a Leader in play at the end of any of the second player’s turns, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match. At the end of six rounds, the player with the most Victory Points wins the match.
